Policy Title

AI Acceptable Use Policy

Effective Date

April 2026

Owner

IT & Security

Classification

1. Purpose and Scope

School Technology Associates, Inc. ("School Technology") is deploying Claude Teams, an enterprise AI assistant, to support staff productivity and workflow improvement. This policy governs the use of Claude and any other IT-approved AI tools by all School Technology employees.

The purpose of this policy is to protect the organization, its customers, and its employees from the risks associated with improper AI use - specifically the unintended disclosure of sensitive, confidential, or regulated data to third-party AI systems.


This policy applies to:

  • All School Technology employees who use IT-approved AI tools

  • All devices - company-owned and personal - used to access AI tools in connection with School Technology work

  • All AI tools, whether accessed through Cowork, a web browser, or a mobile application

2. Definitions

Term

Definition

AI Tool

Any artificial intelligence assistant or automation platform, including but not limited to Claude, used to assist with work tasks.

Approved AI Tool

An AI tool that has been reviewed, provisioned, and authorized by IT. Currently: Claude Teams (via Cowork) and the tools built on it, plus Granola for AI meeting notes and transcription.

Restricted Data

Any data category defined in the AI Restricted Data Reference Guide as prohibited or requiring special handling when used with AI tools.

Shadow AI

Any AI tool used for work purposes that has not been approved by IT. Examples: personal ChatGPT accounts, free Gemini, other browser-based AI tools.

Disclosure Incident

Any actual or suspected entry of restricted data into an AI tool, whether intentional or accidental.

3.3 Connectors

Connectors let an approved AI tool reach another system, such as your calendar, your mail, or your meeting notes. What you may connect today:

Granola - connect it. It is approved and it is the interface we want people using for meeting notes.

Google Drive - do not connect. Drive access is restricted. The company Drive holds files going back many years that need auditing before any AI tool is given access to them.

Gmail - do not connect it yet. It is not restricted outright, because there are uses we expect to enable later, but hold off until IT says otherwise.

This is a starting position, not a permanent one. It will be revisited as the rollout progresses. If a connector would genuinely help your work, ask IT rather than connecting it.

4. Permitted Uses

The following uses of approved AI tools are permitted:


  • Drafting and editing: Writing emails, documents, proposals, letters, announcements, and other business communications

  • Research: Looking up publicly available information, summarizing topics, answering general knowledge questions

  • Document creation: Generating formatted reports, presentations, spreadsheets, and help center articles

  • Summarization: Summarizing meeting notes, articles, policies, or documents that do not contain restricted data

  • Template development: Creating reusable templates for common documents and communications

  • Troubleshooting guidance: Using the STA Support Chat or general AI assistance to diagnose and resolve product or technical issues

  • Process improvement: Identifying inefficiencies, brainstorming solutions, and structuring workflows

  • Tool building: IT-authorized staff using The Architect to design, build, test, and maintain AI tools for the organization


When in doubt about whether a use is permitted, ask IT before proceeding. It is always better to ask first than to report an incident afterward.

5. Prohibited Uses

The following uses are strictly prohibited. Violations may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination, and may trigger regulatory reporting obligations.


5.1 Restricted Data Entry

Staff may not enter the following categories of data into any AI tool, approved or otherwise. The complete list is defined in the AI Restricted Data Reference Guide. Key categories include:

  • Social Security numbers, government-issued ID numbers, passport numbers

  • Full employee payroll figures tied to named individuals

  • Health, medical, or benefits information for named individuals

  • Student records or student-identifiable information

  • System credentials: passwords, API keys, authentication tokens, login details

  • Full financial account numbers (bank, credit card, payment processing)

  • Confidential customer contract pricing or renewal terms tied to named accounts

  • Internal network diagrams, system inventories, or vulnerability details


5.2 Unauthorized Actions

  • Using any AI tool not on the approved list for School Technology work purposes

  • Sharing your Claude Teams account credentials with any other person

  • Attempting to use AI to bypass, circumvent, or test security controls

  • Using AI tools to generate content intended to deceive customers, partners, or employees

  • Entering confidential information about competitors, litigation, or legal strategy without legal review


The "Stranger Test" - a quick way to decide if something is safe to enter: If you would not paste this information into an email to a stranger, do not paste it into an AI tool.

5.3 Publishing and Sharing

Publishing an artifact makes it public to the internet. Publishing is not the same as sharing. When you publish an artifact, anyone with the link can view and interact with it, including people who are not signed in and people outside School Technology. There is no Team or Enterprise restriction on published artifacts.

School Technology generates artifacts constantly - reports, checklists, Cowork outputs - so this is a one-click risk on work you do every day.

Never publish an artifact containing customer, district, student, employee or financial data.

Unpublishing is one-way. Once you unpublish an artifact you cannot publish that same artifact again.

Sharing a chat is different. From a School Technology work account a shared chat is visible only to other members of the organisation, not publicly. From a personal Claude account (Free, Pro or Max) a shared chat IS public to anyone with the link. Keep work in the work account.

Sources: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9547008-publish-and-share-artifacts and https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10593882-share-and-unshare-chats

6. Special Provisions - HR

Due to the nature of HR work, which involves highly sensitive employee data, HR staff are subject to additional restrictions and are required to complete HR-specific data handling training before their account is activated.


6.1 Privacy Assurance

Corrected 2026-08-20. An earlier version of this section said the Claude Teams administrator cannot read individual conversation content and that conversation privacy is protected by the platform design. That was not true. The Primary Owner of the School Technology Team organisation can request a data export which may contain conversations with Claude, uploaded files, and usage patterns. Adam Baker is Primary Owner. Cowork activity is additionally captured in the Compliance API. Treat anything you type into an AI tool as reviewable by School Technology, and keep confidential HR matters out of the AI tools entirely. Verified 2026-08-20 against Anthropic's privacy documentation: https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/9265372-who-owns-and-manages-the-data-of-my-team


6.2 Additional HR Restrictions

  • Employee names must not be paired with salary, health, disciplinary, or identification information in the same AI prompt

  • FMLA, medical accommodation, and disability-related information must be anonymized before use with AI tools

  • I-9 documentation and government ID details may not be entered in any form

  • Performance improvement plans, written warnings, and termination discussions should use role descriptions, not names


6.3 Anonymization Requirement

HR staff are required to anonymize employee-specific information before entering it into an AI tool. Refer to the AI Restricted Data Reference Guide for detailed examples of how to properly anonymize HR data.

7. Shadow AI, Unauthorized Tools, and Browser Extensions

7.1 Shadow AI

Shadow AI - the use of personal or unauthorized AI tools for work purposes - creates significant risk for School Technology, including uncontrolled data exposure, lack of audit trail, and potential regulatory violation.


  • Prohibited examples: Using a personal ChatGPT account to draft a proposal that contains customer names or pricing. Using a free AI tool on a personal device to process internal documents. Using any browser-based AI tool that has not been reviewed and approved by IT.


If you believe a tool not on the approved list would be genuinely useful for School Technology work, contact IT to request a review. IT will evaluate the tool's data handling practices and determine if it can be approved.


The problem with shadow AI is not the tool itself - it's that we have no visibility into where your data goes, how long it is retained, or whether it is used for model training. Only approved tools carry those assurances.

To be clear about what this section does and does not require. School Technology does not restrict personal or free AI tools, and does not ask staff to disable AI features built into other products. Controlling them is not realistic and is not the goal. What is prohibited is the data, not the tool: restricted data must not be entered into any tool that has not been approved for it. Beyond that, if you find a tool that does something well, try it and tell IT what you found.


7.2 Browser Extensions

Browser extensions that interact with, read, or modify Claude Chat (claude.ai) are not permitted without prior IT approval. This includes extensions that:

  • Inject content into Claude's interface or read Claude's responses

  • Claim to enhance, extend, or add features to Claude

  • Capture or log AI conversations

  • Connect Claude to other services or automate Claude actions


The concern is not about browser extensions generally - it is specifically about extensions that sit between you and Claude. An unapproved extension could log your conversations, exfiltrate data, or manipulate Claude's behavior in ways that bypass our controls.


To request approval for a browser extension, contact IT with the extension name and intended use. IT will review it and respond within a reasonable timeframe.


IT Note: Browser extension enforcement is managed through Google Workspace Admin Console (Chrome Browser Cloud Management).

Extensions can be blocked org-wide or whitelisted on a per-extension basis.

This is a Phase 0 configuration task and should be completed before staff accounts are activated.

8. Incident Reporting

If you believe you have accidentally entered restricted data into an AI tool, or if you are aware of a potential policy violation, you must report it immediately.


How to Report

  1. Contact IT immediately - do not wait

  2. Describe what was entered, in which tool, and approximately when

  3. Do not attempt to delete or modify the conversation to cover the incident - this makes investigation harder

  4. IT will assess whether a formal data breach notification is required


School Technology will not penalize staff who self-report accidental incidents in good faith. Proactive reporting allows us to respond quickly and limit any potential harm.


Failure to report a known incident is considered a separate and more serious violation than the original incident.

9. Enforcement

Violations of this policy will be handled in accordance with School Technology's standard disciplinary procedures. Enforcement actions may include:

  • Verbal or written warning for first-time, minor violations (e.g., entering low-risk data without intent)

  • Formal written warning and mandatory retraining for significant violations

  • Suspension of AI tool access pending investigation for serious violations

  • Termination for willful, repeated, or high-impact violations


Violations that result in regulatory exposure - such as the disclosure of student records, employee PII, or protected health information - may also carry legal consequences independent of any disciplinary action taken by School Technology.

10. Policy Review

This policy will be reviewed:

  • Annually, at minimum

  • Before each new phase of the AI rollout (Phase 2 and Phase 3)

  • Whenever a new AI tool is added to the approved list

  • Following any disclosure incident


All staff will be notified of material changes to this policy. Updated versions will be distributed and re-acknowledgment may be required depending on the significance of the changes.
